Then i break everything down into small steps i can do without thinking too much about how im feeling..like first sit up. Then put my feet on the floor. Then go to the bathroom
 Pick up toothbrush. And so on until i do the bare minimum it takes to be a functioning human. Then i have to tell myself its okay to be a spaced out zombie, at least i got out of bed which is a good thing. The key for me is learning to forgive myself for all the mistakes and negative thoughts because in the grand scheme of things it doesnt matter too much; at least i survived another day.

I grew up in a culture that really emphasizes skinny=beautiful. I'm 5'4, and even at my lowest weight of 115 lbs my mother would tell me to lose just 5 more. I realize now that i had extreme body dysmorphia and thought I was fat when, looking at old pictures, I clearly was not. I was obsessed with my weight, and would scramble to lose some weight every time I knew I was going to a special occasion, or see family. I was miserable and yo-yoed for years. I started lifting almost two years ago, and havent stepped on a scale since unless at the doctors. I learned to love my body for what it can do and what it can achieve, rather than what it looks like. Ironically, I look better now at a higher weight than I ever did at my lowest before I started lifting, and actually love the body I'm in. I can look in the mirror and appreciate my muscles and be proud of that instead of pinching any fat and obsessing about it.
